overall: Tomorrow (Sunday, June 22) in Atlanta is expected to be a mostly sunny day with only a slight chance of afternoon/evening showers or thunderstorms after 5pm (20% PoP), making it largely a dry day. Temperatures will rebound sharply from today's anomalously cool observed max of 73.4°F, which was suppressed by cloud cover and precipitation. Conditions broadly favor a hot summer day with seasonably high temperatures.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance shows moderate spread: ECMWF and GFS are on the cooler end (~85.4–85.8°F), while HRRR, NBM, and Weather.com cluster higher at ~87–89°F, and the NWS official narrative targets a high near 89°F. The full ensemble expected TMAX of 84.6°F is being dragged downward by today's unusually low observed max (73.4°F), an artifact of heavy cloud cover and storms today rather than a true thermodynamic signal — the forecast-only model (89.2°F), which ignores that prior obs, likely better reflects tomorrow's potential.
max_temp_prediction: The most probable single bucket in the full ensemble is 90–91°F at 34.3%, and the NWS and forecast-only model both target near 89°F, suggesting the true high is most likely in the upper 80s to near 90°F. The full ensemble's lower expected value of 84.6°F reflects distortion from today's anomalous obs and should be discounted; the preponderance of model evidence (HRRR 88.6°F, NBM 88.2°F, NWS 89°F, FO model 89.2°F) supports a high in the 88–90°F range. Confidence is moderate-to-good for this range given the mostly sunny setup and low PoP through most of the day.
